profiles.label: Web application
profiles.summary: Responsive browser surfaces with pointer, keyboard, forms, navigation, and asynchronous feedback.

specimens.title: Responsive application workspace
specimens.purpose: Prove hierarchy, navigation, primary action, and responsive reflow with representative content.

specimens.title: Forms and action hierarchy
specimens.purpose: Prove labels, control anatomy, focus, validation, disabled behavior, and action priority.

specimens.title: Collection and asynchronous feedback
specimens.purpose: Prove real data volume, status language, empty/error recovery, and progressive updates.

data_scenarios.data_condition: No records exist or the active filters match nothing.
data_scenarios.expectation: Explain the empty condition, preserve active filters, and expose the next useful action.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Representative and maximum-density records are available.
data_scenarios.expectation: Preserve hierarchy, action availability, and scanability without layout shift.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Some records are stale, still loading, or unavailable.
data_scenarios.expectation: Distinguish usable from pending content and preserve retry, selection, and scroll context.

data_scenarios.data_condition: A request fails, permission is limited, or the client is offline.
data_scenarios.expectation: Keep confirmed data and unsaved input, explain the cause, and expose safe retry or recovery.

content_constraints: Support labels and actions at 200% text zoom without truncation.
Keep table cells, validation, and recovery copy understandable with long localized values.
component_contract.iconography: Use the product icon set with text labels for unfamiliar, destructive, permission, and recovery actions; never rely on shape or color alone.

interaction_matrix.trigger: Click, double activation, hover, drag, or context-menu invocation on an enabled target.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve pointerdown, any pointermove beyond the drag threshold, and pointerup/click as one gesture; treat pointercancel, capture loss, or release outside the valid target as cancellation.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Show pressed, selected, drag-preview, drop-target, or context-menu feedback within the immediate response budget without implying completion.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Move focus only when the native control or documented composite pattern requires it; preserve visible focus, selection, scroll anchor, and the invoking target across transient layers.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Distinguish single, double, held, and repeated activation; debounce or reject duplicate consequential actions while preserving legitimate repeated controls.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Pointercancel, Escape during a captured gesture, invalid drop, or release outside restores the last committed state and removes transient feedback.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: While work is pending, keep status and cancel/retry affordances perceivable, block only conflicting activation, and never convert a pending press into duplicate submission.

interaction_matrix.surface: Web application controls, navigation, dialogs, and collections
interaction_matrix.trigger: Tab or arrow navigation followed by Enter, Space, Escape, or the documented shortcut.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve keydown and keyup according to the native control pattern, synthesize one activation, and reserve Tab, arrows, Escape, Enter, and Space for the focused context without browser-shortcut conflict.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Expose visible focus before activation and show pressed, expanded, selected, pending, or validation feedback without waiting for key release when the platform pattern requires an immediate response.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Keep focus visible and ordered, contain modal focus, restore the invoker after dismissal, and preserve the active descendant and scroll position through rerenders.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Ignore operating-system key repeat for single-submit actions while allowing documented repeat for navigation, stepping, scrolling, or continuous controls.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Escape or the documented cancel command closes only the top cancellable context, restores focus, and leaves committed state unchanged; keyboard traps are forbidden.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Announce pending state once, retain a stable focus target, suppress conflicting shortcuts or duplicate activation, and expose safe cancellation or retry when available.

editing_matrix.surface: Web forms, search, filters, and inline editable controls
editing_matrix.composition_behavior: Preserve the IME composition buffer and do not validate, format, submit, or invoke character shortcuts until composition commits.
editing_matrix.paste_autofill_behavior: Accept paste, browser autofill, password-manager, and dictation updates through native input events; preserve the entered value and expose intentional normalization.
editing_matrix.selection_caret_behavior: Preserve selection, caret, scroll, and text direction through rerenders, suggestions, masking, asynchronous feedback, and focus return.
editing_matrix.formatting_behavior: Parse locale-aware values without rewriting partial input; apply destructive trimming, masking, or canonical formatting only at a documented boundary without moving the caret unexpectedly.
editing_matrix.validation_timing: Do not validate during IME composition; validate at the documented blur, change, or submit boundary and update an already exposed error as soon as the value becomes valid.
editing_matrix.validation_feedback: Associate concise error and correction text with the field, retain the value, expose a summary only when useful, and announce each material change once without color alone.
editing_matrix.dirty_state_behavior: Distinguish unchanged, dirty, saving, saved, and failed values; warn on navigation only when confirmed user input would be lost.
editing_matrix.persistence_behavior: For manual save or autosave, expose ownership and freshness, retain safe drafts across retry, refresh, offline recovery, and session renewal, and never claim unsaved work is saved.
editing_matrix.undo_redo_behavior: Preserve native text undo/redo and provide bounded application undo for committed reversible edits without corrupting selection or newer changes.
editing_matrix.conflict_behavior: Detect stale, multi-tab, or remote edit conflict before overwrite; show the competing version and offer explicit reload, keep, compare, or merge recovery.
editing_matrix.read_only_disabled_behavior: Keep read-only values selectable and understandable, remove disabled controls from activation, and state why an action is disabled and what can enable it.
editing_matrix.submission_behavior: Define Enter and multiline behavior, validate before side effects, prevent duplicate submission while pending, preserve values on failure, and bind success to the authoritative response.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: No records exist or active filters match nothing.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Distinguish first-use from no-results, preserve filters, and offer the next useful create, import, or reset action.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Representative and maximum-density records, long values, and mixed statuses are present.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Keep hierarchy, action availability, selection, and scanability stable without layout shift or silent truncation.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Cached records remain usable while pages, mutations, or dependent regions are loading or stale.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Mark freshness and pending regions locally, retain usable content and input, and prevent out-of-order responses from overwriting newer state.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Network, permission, session, validation, or server failure blocks the requested result.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Explain the bounded cause, preserve confirmed data and unsaved input, place errors near the affected control or region, and expose a safe recovery path.

accessibility_matrix.reading_order: DOM reading order follows the visible task hierarchy before responsive visual rearrangement.
accessibility_matrix.focus_order: Focus follows task order, enters contained overlays deliberately, and returns to the invoking control after dismissal.
keyboard: Complete every primary task without a pointer.
Use standard Tab, arrow, Enter, Space, and Escape behavior without keyboard traps.
announcements: Announce validation at the affected field.
Announce loading completion, errors, and asynchronous collection changes without stealing focus.
accessibility_matrix.target_size: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA target-size requirements, using at least 24x24 CSS px or documented spacing exceptions.
accessibility_matrix.contrast: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in light, dark, high-contrast, hover, focus, disabled, and error combinations.
accessibility_matrix.zoom_reflow: Reflow at 400% zoom and 200% text size without two-dimensional page scrolling, loss of content, or hidden controls.
alternatives: Provide text equivalents for icons and meaningful images.
Provide non-drag and non-color alternatives for every action and status.

navigation_matrix.entry: Application URL, navigation item, notification link, or preserved browser history entry.
navigation_matrix.destination: The named route, selected record, state, or task step with required context restored.
navigation_matrix.trigger: Pointer or keyboard activation, browser back/forward, or a validated deep link.
navigation_matrix.back_behavior: Return to the prior meaningful route and restore filters, selection, scroll position, and safe draft state.
navigation_matrix.deep_link_behavior: Open the intended authorized object or state directly; otherwise show a bounded missing, expired, or permission outcome without leaking data.
navigation_matrix.interruption_recovery: After refresh, session renewal, connectivity loss, or external update, restore the last safe checkpoint and reconcile stale actions explicitly.

content_matrix.purpose: Help the user understand context and complete one primary job.
content_matrix.copy: Use concrete labels and verbs that match the user's domain; keep supporting text scannable and place prerequisites before action.
content_matrix.primary_action: Name the outcome rather than the gesture and keep one dominant action per task region.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Show consequence, scope, ownership, freshness, and irreversible effects before commitment.
content_matrix.localization: Support right-to-left layout, locale-aware dates, numbers, names, and at least 30% text expansion without semantic truncation.
content_limits: Keep button labels concise but never replace meaning with an unlabeled icon.
Wrap long names and identifiers or expose their full value on focus without obscuring controls.

content_matrix.surface: Web empty, error, permission, and destructive states
content_matrix.purpose: Explain what happened, what remains safe, and the next available action.
content_matrix.copy: Use specific, non-blaming language with the failed scope and a useful recovery step.
content_matrix.primary_action: Offer retry, revise, request access, undo, or return only when that action is safe and available.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Never imply success before confirmation; identify retained data, destructive consequences, and whether retry can duplicate work.
content_matrix.localization: Keep recovery meaning intact under translation, plural rules, right-to-left order, and locale-specific support references.
content_limits: Do not expose secrets, internal stack traces, or inaccessible object names.
Keep the essential cause and recovery action visible before expandable diagnostics.

motion_contract.purpose: Use motion to preserve spatial continuity, confirm direct manipulation, and reveal asynchronous state without delaying work.

transitions.surface: Web controls, overlays, collections, and responsive layout
transitions.trigger: Direct activation, overlay entry or exit, collection update, or responsive reflow.
transitions.response: Animate only the affected relationship while feedback and final state remain perceivable without motion.
transitions.interrupt_behavior: A new input cancels or retargets from the current visual state without queuing, focus loss, duplicate action, or stale completion.

motion_contract.reduced_motion: Remove spatial travel, parallax, and nonessential stagger; use immediate state changes, opacity, and persistent status text while preserving sequence and feedback.

methods: target-user task session for high-consequence or unfamiliar flows
critical_tasks: Reach the intended route from navigation or a deep link.
Complete and recover the primary data-changing action.
Understand empty, partial, error, and permission outcomes.
success_criteria: Participants complete the primary task without moderator rescue.
No critical accessibility blocker or unrecoverable context loss remains.
Users can state the consequence and recovery path before a high-consequence action.

targets.label: compact web
targets.adaptation: Navigation condenses, the primary task stays first, and controls remain operable without horizontal scrolling.
targets.stretch_behavior: Reflow continuously to the supported minimum while preserving focus, selection, scroll position, and unsaved input.
targets.overflow_behavior: Wrap or internally scroll bounded content; never clip primary actions or introduce page-level horizontal scrolling.

targets.label: regular web
targets.adaptation: Navigation, content, and secondary context share the viewport without changing task priority.
targets.stretch_behavior: Redistribute columns between compact and wide thresholds without resetting active interaction state.
targets.overflow_behavior: Keep long text, dense tables, menus, and dialogs operable through bounded wrapping or scrolling.

targets.label: wide web
targets.adaptation: Additional width improves scanability and context rather than stretching the reading measure.
targets.stretch_behavior: Cap reading measure and use surplus width for approved context without diluting task hierarchy.
targets.overflow_behavior: Constrain panes and collections independently so dense content cannot push primary controls off screen.

profiles.label: Mobile application
profiles.summary: Touch-first compact surfaces with safe areas, orientation changes, software keyboards, and native navigation patterns.

specimens.title: Touch-first task flow
specimens.purpose: Prove safe areas, thumb-reachable actions, compact navigation, and task continuity.

specimens.title: Mobile input and keyboard
specimens.purpose: Prove touch targets, validation, keyboard-open layout, and focus visibility.

specimens.title: System feedback and interruption
specimens.purpose: Prove transient feedback, sheets, empty/error recovery, and reduced-motion behavior.

data_scenarios.data_condition: No local or remote items are available.
data_scenarios.expectation: Show a first useful action without obscuring navigation or safe-area affordances.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Representative and dense mobile content is available.
data_scenarios.expectation: Keep touch targets reachable and preserve selection across navigation and rotation.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Cached content is visible while a refresh or upload is pending.
data_scenarios.expectation: Identify pending content and preserve optimistic actions, retry identity, and input.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Permission, connectivity, or a request prevents completion.
data_scenarios.expectation: Explain the boundary, retain safe local work, and provide retry, settings, or recovery actions.

content_constraints: Keep essential labels and actions visible with dynamic type and the software keyboard open.
Support long localized labels without shrinking touch targets or relying on truncation.
component_contract.iconography: Use platform-familiar symbols with accessible labels and text reinforcement for destructive, permission, navigation, and recovery actions.

interaction_matrix.surface: Mobile navigation, controls, lists, and sheets
interaction_matrix.trigger: Tap, long press, swipe, or drag within an identified interactive target.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve touch down, movement against platform slop and scroll thresholds, and touch up as one gesture; treat system takeover, pointercancel, app suspension, or rotation as cancellation or safe interruption.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Show pressed, selected, drag, reorder, or sheet feedback immediately with haptics only as a redundant cue, never as the sole confirmation.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Preserve the active control, reading position, selection, safe-area visibility, and software-keyboard relationship without stealing accessibility focus.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Distinguish tap, double tap, long press, and held repeat; gate repeated consequential taps while keeping intentional stepping controls responsive.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Crossing the scroll threshold, leaving the valid drop region, system gesture takeover, or explicit cancel restores the last committed state and provides a simple non-gesture alternative.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Keep progress and interruption state visible, prevent duplicate commitment, preserve the task through suspension, and expose cancel, retry, or resume at a safe boundary.

interaction_matrix.trigger: Focus traversal, external-keyboard activation, screen-reader action, software-keyboard submit, or dismissal.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve hardware keydown/keyup, software-keyboard action, switch command, or assistive activation exactly once using the platform control semantics.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Expose focus, pressed, selected, validation, or pending state immediately and announce the change without duplicating the screen-reader gesture announcement.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Keep the focused control visible above the keyboard and safe areas, contain sheets deliberately, and restore focus after sheets, permission prompts, or system interruptions close.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Ignore key repeat and repeated assistive activation for single-submit actions while supporting documented navigation and stepper repetition.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: The platform back, Escape, dismiss action, or assistive cancel closes the nearest cancellable context without discarding committed or unsaved work silently.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Retain a reachable status and focus target, block only conflicting actions, prevent duplicate submit, and announce safe retry, cancel, or resume choices.

editing_matrix.surface: Mobile forms, search, messages, and inline editing
editing_matrix.composition_behavior: Keep marked IME text intact, visible above the software keyboard, and free from validation, shortcut, formatting, or submit side effects until composition commits.
editing_matrix.paste_autofill_behavior: Accept paste, one-time-code and contact autofill, password managers, and dictation without clearing the field, duplicating text, or bypassing user-visible constraints.
editing_matrix.selection_caret_behavior: Preserve caret, selection handles, scroll, and focused-field visibility through rotation, keyboard resize, suggestions, sheet changes, and asynchronous updates.
editing_matrix.formatting_behavior: Use the appropriate keyboard and locale parser; tolerate partial numbers, dates, and identifiers and defer canonical formatting until a stable boundary.
editing_matrix.validation_timing: Skip validation during composition, validate at the documented change, focus, or submit boundary, and clear an exposed error promptly after correction.
editing_matrix.validation_feedback: Place actionable text next to the field, announce it once, keep the keyboard and corrected value in context, and never use vibration, icon, or color as the only cue.
editing_matrix.dirty_state_behavior: Expose unchanged, dirty, saving, saved, and failed state and interrupt navigation only when leaving would discard confirmed user input.
editing_matrix.persistence_behavior: Autosave or manual save retains safe local drafts through backgrounding, offline use, permission prompts, sign-in, retry, and process restoration with truthful freshness.
editing_matrix.undo_redo_behavior: Preserve platform text undo/redo and offer a reachable bounded undo for committed reversible edits without replacing newer input.
editing_matrix.conflict_behavior: Detect remote, device, or restored-draft conflicts before overwrite and offer explicit compare, keep local, use remote, or merge recovery.
editing_matrix.read_only_disabled_behavior: Keep read-only content selectable and announced, prevent disabled activation, and expose the reason and enabling action without relying on reduced opacity alone.
editing_matrix.submission_behavior: Define software-keyboard action semantics, distinguish newline from submit, prevent duplicate submission, retain values on failure, and reconcile only the authoritative completion.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: No local or remote items exist for the current context.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Explain whether this is first use or no results and keep one reachable create, scan, import, or reset action.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Representative content, long values, and dense lists are available.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Keep touch targets reachable, use stable row identity, and preserve selection, scroll, and draft state across navigation and rotation.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Cached content remains visible while refresh, upload, synchronization, or optimistic work is pending.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Identify pending items, prevent duplicate submission, preserve retry identity and input, and reconcile late responses without reverting newer state.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Connectivity, permission, authentication, storage, or system service prevents completion.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Retain safe local work, state the boundary, and offer retry, settings, sign-in, storage cleanup, or another valid recovery action.

accessibility_matrix.reading_order: Assistive-technology reading follows the visible task order and excludes obscured background content while a sheet or modal is active.
accessibility_matrix.focus_order: Focus advances through the task, moves into presented surfaces, remains visible above the keyboard, and returns to the invoker on dismissal.
keyboard: Support external keyboard traversal and activation for all primary tasks.
Do not require a multi-pointer or path gesture without a simple alternative.
announcements: Announce validation, permission outcomes, upload progress, completion, and interruption recovery.
Avoid repeated live-region or platform announcement noise during continuous updates.
accessibility_matrix.target_size: Use at least 44pt touch targets with adequate separation and preserve them under dynamic type and orientation change.
accessibility_matrix.contrast: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA or stricter native-platform contrast for text, icons, focus, selected, disabled, and error states.
accessibility_matrix.zoom_reflow: Support platform text scaling and display zoom without clipped content, hidden focus, or actions obscured by safe areas and the software keyboard.
alternatives: Provide text alternatives for meaningful imagery and icons.
Provide non-motion, non-color, non-haptic, and non-gesture equivalents for all meaning and actions.

navigation_matrix.surface: Mobile navigation stack, tabs, sheets, and external links
navigation_matrix.entry: App launch, tab, notification, universal link, widget, or resumed task.
navigation_matrix.destination: The intended authorized screen, object, or task step with navigation context and draft state restored.
navigation_matrix.trigger: Touch, assistive action, keyboard activation, system back gesture, notification, or validated deep link.
navigation_matrix.back_behavior: Follow platform back expectations, dismiss transient layers before leaving the task, and warn before discarding meaningful unsaved work.
navigation_matrix.deep_link_behavior: Open the intended authorized state after required sign-in or permission and provide a safe expired or unavailable destination when resolution fails.
navigation_matrix.interruption_recovery: Resume from calls, permission dialogs, app suspension, process recreation, rotation, or network loss at the last safe checkpoint without duplicate work.

content_matrix.purpose: Make the next task step and its consequence understandable within a compact, interruption-prone context.
content_matrix.copy: Use short domain language, front-load distinguishing words, and keep instructions next to the control that needs them.
content_matrix.primary_action: Use an outcome label and keep the principal action reachable without depending on screen-edge position alone.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Expose permission use, network or storage impact, data destination, and destructive consequences before the system prompt or commitment.
content_matrix.localization: Support right-to-left navigation, locale formats, plural rules, and substantial text expansion under dynamic type.
content_limits: Do not truncate the only distinguishing portion of a title or action.
Move secondary detail behind disclosure while keeping consequence and recovery visible.

content_matrix.surface: Mobile permission, offline, validation, and interruption states
content_matrix.purpose: Explain the interrupted boundary and help the user continue without losing work.
content_matrix.copy: Name the blocked capability and retained work in plain language without blaming the user.
content_matrix.primary_action: Offer the valid next step such as retry, open settings, revise, save locally, or return.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Do not claim upload, payment, save, or deletion success before authoritative confirmation and identify whether retry can duplicate the action.
content_matrix.localization: Keep system-setting names, support instructions, and recovery order correct for locale and platform.
content_limits: Keep the essential cause and action above expandable diagnostics.
Never reveal credentials, private object names, or internal error payloads.

motion_contract.purpose: Use native-feeling motion to preserve navigation and direct-manipulation continuity while keeping interrupted tasks understandable.

transitions.surface: Mobile navigation, sheets, direct manipulation, and asynchronous feedback
transitions.trigger: Screen or sheet transition, gesture completion, orientation change, or operation-state update.
transitions.response: Maintain spatial ownership and final status without delaying the next input or obscuring safe areas and focused fields.
transitions.interrupt_behavior: Retarget or finish safely from the current state when the gesture reverses, the app suspends, orientation changes, or a new action supersedes the transition.

motion_contract.reduced_motion: Replace spatial travel, parallax, zoom, and prolonged spring effects with direct state changes or brief fades while preserving navigation hierarchy and operation feedback.

methods: target-user task sessions across compact devices and interruption scenarios
critical_tasks: Enter from launch or a deep link and complete the primary task one-handed.
Complete input with the software keyboard, dynamic type, and a system permission boundary.
Resume safely after suspension, rotation, offline state, or a failed submission.
success_criteria: Participants complete the primary task without accidental activation or moderator rescue.
No critical content, focus, or action is obscured by safe areas, dynamic type, or the keyboard.
Interruption and retry never lose work or duplicate a high-consequence action.

targets.label: compact mobile portrait
targets.adaptation: Primary actions remain reachable and content clears safe areas and the software keyboard.
targets.stretch_behavior: Reflow around safe areas, text scaling, and the software keyboard without losing focused input or draft content.
targets.overflow_behavior: Use vertical or component-local scrolling and wrapping; never hide critical actions behind the keyboard or cutout.

targets.label: regular mobile portrait
targets.adaptation: The same task gains breathing room without changing navigation or action priority.
targets.stretch_behavior: Expand spacing and content measure without changing navigation, focus, selection, or action priority.
targets.overflow_behavior: Keep long content and dense lists scrollable while pinned navigation and feedback remain visible.

targets.label: mobile landscape
targets.adaptation: Navigation and content adapt to landscape while touch targets and critical actions remain visible.
targets.stretch_behavior: Recompose for the short axis while preserving the active field, selection, scroll anchor, and unsaved work across rotation.
targets.overflow_behavior: Prioritize the active task and use bounded pane or sheet scrolling instead of shrinking touch targets.

profiles.label: Desktop application
profiles.summary: Resizable windowed surfaces with menus, toolbars, multi-pane layouts, pointer precision, and keyboard acceleration.

specimens.title: Window, menu, and toolbar
specimens.purpose: Prove window hierarchy, command discoverability, platform chrome boundaries, and separate disabled behavior from label/indicator/icon appearance; exercise native window actions through their API and permission declarations to an observed system effect.

specimens.title: Keyboard and command workflow
specimens.purpose: Prove focus, shortcuts, command search, selection, and recoverable feedback.

specimens.title: Resizable multi-pane workspace
specimens.purpose: Prove information density, pane priority, selection, and resize behavior.

data_scenarios.data_condition: The workspace or active collection has no items.
data_scenarios.expectation: Preserve pane structure and provide creation, import, or filter-reset actions.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Representative and maximum-density workspace data is available.
data_scenarios.expectation: Keep commands, selection, focus order, and detail context stable at supported densities.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Some panes are loading, stale, or disconnected.
data_scenarios.expectation: Keep usable panes interactive and distinguish pending content without resetting workspace state.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Permission, storage, or network failure blocks a pane or command.
data_scenarios.expectation: Preserve unsaved work and selection while exposing bounded retry, undo, or recovery.

content_constraints: Keep commands distinguishable at compact window sizes and high system text scaling.
Allow long paths, names, shortcuts, and diagnostics to wrap or scroll without moving primary commands.
component_contract.iconography: Follow platform command and file-type conventions, pair unfamiliar or destructive symbols with labels, and preserve meaning in monochrome and high contrast.

interaction_matrix.surface: Desktop panes, toolbars, menus, and direct-manipulation controls
interaction_matrix.trigger: Click, double-click, context click, hover, drag, drop, or pane resize.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve pointerdown, pointermove with platform drag or resize threshold, and pointerup as one captured operation; pointercancel, capture loss, invalid drop, or window deactivation interrupts safely.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Show pressed, selection, hover intent, drag preview, insertion point, valid drop region, or resize bounds before any committed mutation.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Distinguish focus, selection, and active pane; preserve command context, scroll, and unsaved state when menus, dialogs, or secondary windows open and close.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Distinguish single click, double-click, held buttons, and repeated commands; reject duplicate consequential activation without breaking continuous resize or stepping.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Escape, pointercancel, invalid drop, or release outside the capture region restores the last committed geometry or data and clears transient state.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Keep the initiating object and operation status identifiable, prevent conflicting edits, and expose safe cancel, queue, retry, or background continuation behavior.

interaction_matrix.surface: Desktop commands, menus, dialogs, panes, and collections
interaction_matrix.trigger: Tab or directional navigation, mnemonic, Enter, Space, Escape, or documented application and system shortcut.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve keydown/keyup, mnemonic, chord, and command routing through the active window and pane exactly once without conflicting with operating-system shortcuts.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Show focus, command availability, pressed, selected, pending, or rejected-shortcut feedback within the active command context.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Keep focus and selection visible, contain modal focus, preserve the active descendant across pane updates, and restore the prior command context after dismissal.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Use key repeat only for documented navigation, stepping, scrolling, or continuous commands and suppress it for destructive or single-submit actions.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Escape or the platform cancel command unwinds only the nearest cancellable menu, dialog, drag, or command mode and restores its invoker.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Keep command status and cancellation reachable, prevent conflicting shortcuts or duplicate execution, and describe whether work continues in the foreground or background.

editing_matrix.surface: Desktop documents, properties, search, tables, and multi-pane editors
editing_matrix.composition_behavior: Preserve IME marked text and command context; suspend validation, accelerators, formatting, and save submission until composition commits.
editing_matrix.paste_autofill_behavior: Accept plain, rich, multiline, drag-inserted, and autofilled content through an explicit import policy with a preview or fallback when formatting would be lost.
editing_matrix.selection_caret_behavior: Preserve caret, multi-selection, active cell, scroll, and pane ownership through rerenders, background work, window changes, and command execution.
editing_matrix.formatting_behavior: Keep partial locale values editable, separate display formatting from stored value, and do not reformat or move the caret during an active edit.
editing_matrix.validation_timing: Do not validate during composition; validate at the documented cell, field, document, or save boundary and keep correction local to the active editing context.
editing_matrix.validation_feedback: Show specific field or document errors, maintain an inspectable problem list when useful, announce state changes, and retain the invalid value for correction.
editing_matrix.dirty_state_behavior: Show dirty ownership per document or pane and distinguish saving, saved, failed, external change, and recovered draft before close or replacement.
editing_matrix.persistence_behavior: Manual save or autosave uses atomic recovery, names the stored version and location, preserves drafts after crash or storage failure, and never silently overwrites.
editing_matrix.undo_redo_behavior: Maintain coherent native and application undo/redo groups across typing, paste, formatting, and reversible commands while excluding unrelated remote updates.
editing_matrix.conflict_behavior: Detect file, process, remote, or multi-window edit conflict and offer compare, merge, save as, keep, or reload without destroying either version.
editing_matrix.read_only_disabled_behavior: Allow selection and copy in read-only views, prevent disabled commands, and explain permission, selection, lock, or state prerequisites in the current command context.
editing_matrix.submission_behavior: Define Enter, commit, apply, save, and close separately; block duplicate commits while pending, preserve edits on failure, and accept only the authoritative result.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: The workspace, file, selection, or active collection has no content.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Preserve window and pane structure, explain the scope, and expose valid create, open, import, or filter-reset commands.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Representative and maximum-density files, rows, metadata, and command states are available.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Keep selection identity, keyboard order, command enablement, and detail context stable through sorting, resizing, and pane changes.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Some panes, indexes, synchronizations, or background operations are loading, stale, or disconnected.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Keep usable panes interactive, mark pending ownership locally, and prevent background completion from stealing focus or replacing newer edits.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Permission, storage, file conflict, dependency, or network failure blocks a pane or command.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Preserve selection and unsaved work, identify the affected resource, and expose retry, save-as, resolve-conflict, undo, or another bounded recovery.

semantics: menu, toolbar, tree, grid, and dialog relationships
accessibility_matrix.reading_order: Accessibility order follows window hierarchy and active-pane task order rather than paint or z-index order.
accessibility_matrix.focus_order: Keyboard focus moves predictably across chrome and panes, remains distinct from selection, is contained by modal dialogs, and returns to the invoking command.
keyboard: Expose every command through standard keyboard navigation or a documented shortcut.
Provide keyboard alternatives for drag, resize, context menus, and pointer-precision actions.
announcements: Announce command results, file conflicts, progress completion, and errors without stealing focus.
Expose selected item, sort state, expanded state, and active pane through native accessibility APIs.
accessibility_matrix.target_size: Meet the platform target-size convention and at least WCAG 2.2 AA 24x24 CSS px equivalent where pointer targets apply.
accessibility_matrix.contrast: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA and operating-system high-contrast requirements for text, icons, focus, selection, disabled, and error states.
accessibility_matrix.zoom_reflow: Honor operating-system text and display scaling, window resizing, and 400% content zoom without clipped commands or loss of task access.
alternatives: Provide text names for icons, previews, and status indicators.
Provide non-drag, non-color, non-audio, and non-motion alternatives for every operation and state.

navigation_matrix.surface: Desktop windows, workspaces, panes, menus, and documents
navigation_matrix.entry: Application launch, recent item, file association, command, notification, or restored session.
navigation_matrix.destination: The intended workspace, document, pane, selection, or modal task with command context restored.
navigation_matrix.trigger: Pointer, keyboard command, file open, window switch, history action, or operating-system deep link.
navigation_matrix.back_behavior: Use application history only where meaningful, close transient layers before documents, and confirm or preserve unsaved changes before leaving context.
navigation_matrix.deep_link_behavior: Open the authorized resource and exact stable subcontext when supported; otherwise expose a bounded missing, moved, conflicting, or permission state.
navigation_matrix.interruption_recovery: Recover after sleep, crash, file-system change, external edit, device removal, or reconnect using the last safe saved or autosaved checkpoint and explicit conflict resolution.

content_matrix.purpose: Support expert scanning and efficient command execution without hiding consequence or context.
content_matrix.copy: Use stable domain nouns, verb-first commands, visible shortcuts, and concise status text tied to the affected resource.
content_matrix.primary_action: Keep the current task's principal command visually and semantically distinct while preserving menu and shortcut access.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Show active file or object, save state, conflict ownership, scope, and irreversible consequences before commitment.
content_matrix.localization: Support right-to-left panes, locale formats, system font scaling, translated menus, and long paths or identifiers.
content_limits: Middle-elide paths only when the beginning and filename remain distinguishable and the full path is accessible.
Do not encode command availability or selection using icon or color alone.

content_matrix.surface: Desktop conflict, failure, and destructive dialogs
content_matrix.purpose: Help the user understand affected resources and recover without losing work.
content_matrix.copy: Name the resource, retained state, conflict or failure boundary, and consequence of each option.
content_matrix.primary_action: Prefer retry, save copy, merge, restore, undo, or cancel according to data safety rather than button position.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Never overwrite, close, publish, or delete without accurately representing save state, external changes, and recoverability.
content_matrix.localization: Preserve resource identity and option distinctions across translation, right-to-left order, and system dialog conventions.
content_limits: Keep essential consequence and safe default visible without expanding technical detail.
Place diagnostics behind a copyable detail view without exposing secrets.

motion_contract.purpose: Use restrained motion to connect panes, commands, overlays, and direct manipulation while preserving expert speed and system conventions.

transitions.surface: Desktop panes, menus, overlays, selection, and direct manipulation
transitions.trigger: Pane change, overlay open or close, selection update, drag or resize completion, or background-state change.
transitions.response: Clarify ownership and destination without delaying keyboard use or moving unrelated workspace regions.
transitions.interrupt_behavior: New keyboard or pointer input cancels, retargets, or completes from the current state without queued commands, focus theft, or lost selection.

motion_contract.reduced_motion: Disable spatial travel, parallax, and nonessential interpolation; retain immediate final state, focus, selection, progress, and status text.

methods: target-user workflow session with dense data and window-resize stress
critical_tasks: Open or restore a workspace and locate the intended resource.
Complete the primary command using pointer and keyboard paths.
Recover unsaved work or resolve an external-change, storage, or permission conflict.
success_criteria: Experts complete the primary workflow without shortcut conflict or unintended context switch.
Focus, selection, and unsaved state survive resize, dialog, and background updates.
Users correctly choose a safe recovery option for conflicts and destructive operations.

targets.label: compact desktop window
targets.adaptation: Secondary panes collapse or narrow without hiding the active command or task.
targets.stretch_behavior: Resize panes continuously to the supported minimum while preserving focus, selection, scroll anchors, and unsaved edits.
targets.overflow_behavior: Collapse secondary context or add pane-local scrolling; never clip the active command, dialog, or recovery path.

targets.label: wide desktop window
targets.adaptation: Additional panes and context become visible while keyboard order and reading measure remain stable.
targets.stretch_behavior: Expose approved context as space grows without changing keyboard order or resetting pane state.
targets.overflow_behavior: Keep dense collections and details independently scrollable with stable headers, selection, and commands.

profiles.label: Command-line interface
profiles.summary: Line-oriented commands that remain understandable in TTY, piped, narrow, no-color, success, progress, and failure contexts.

specimens.title: Invocation and help
specimens.purpose: Prove command grammar, hierarchy, examples, wrapping, and discoverability without relying on color.

specimens.title: Success and failure outcomes
specimens.purpose: Prove terminal success, recoverable error, fatal error, exit meaning, and actionable next steps.

specimens.title: Progress, cancellation, and piping
specimens.purpose: Prove live progress, cancellation, stable piped output, and diagnostics separation.

anatomy: TTY progress and stable piped output

data_scenarios.data_condition: No input or matching result is available.
data_scenarios.expectation: Produce an explicit empty outcome with a stable exit meaning and actionable next step.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Representative and high-volume results are produced.
data_scenarios.expectation: Preserve deterministic ordering, machine-readable output, and human scanability.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Some work succeeds before interruption or per-item failure.
data_scenarios.expectation: Separate completed, pending, and failed items and preserve retry identity.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Permission, network, configuration, or dependency access fails.
data_scenarios.expectation: Use a stable exit code, keep stdout clean for piping, and place recovery diagnostics on the correct channel.

content_constraints: Preserve parseable stdout and place diagnostics on stderr when output is piped.
Wrap human-readable text at narrow widths without truncating identifiers, commands, or recovery steps.
component_contract.iconography: Use textual status words and conventional ASCII or Unicode marks only as redundant cues; every outcome remains complete in no-color and plain-text output.

interaction_matrix.trigger: Invoke the documented command with valid, missing, conflicting, repeated, or malformed arguments and environment input.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Read argv, environment, stdin mode, and terminal capability; parse and validate deterministically before side effects, then emit output and one stable exit status.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Return actionable usage or validation output immediately for rejected input and emit an explicit start or progress signal before a long-running accepted operation.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Preserve terminal ownership, cursor placement, input echo policy, and the caller's ability to distinguish stdout, stderr, and the final prompt.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Define idempotency, overwrite, append, or duplicate rejection for repeated invocation and never multiply side effects because output is retried or a terminal reconnects.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Signals, closed stdin, or documented cancel requests stop at a safe boundary, restore terminal state, and report partial work plus the exact resume or cleanup action.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: For long work, emit bounded progress without corrupting machine output, accept documented cancellation, and never prompt when non-interactive mode is requested.

interaction_matrix.surface: Interactive CLI prompt and running operation
interaction_matrix.trigger: Enter a choice, request help, send end-of-input, or cancel with the platform interrupt sequence.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Process keydown-derived terminal input as complete documented choices, line editing, help, end-of-input, or an interrupt; never act on incomplete escape or composition sequences.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Echo, mask, validate, or acknowledge input immediately and keep prompts, errors, progress, and results distinguishable in color and no-color modes.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Keep one clear input owner, preserve the editable buffer and cursor across redraws, and return the terminal cursor and mode cleanly on every exit.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Treat repeated Enter, repeated choice keys, and terminal key repeat according to the prompt contract and suppress duplicate consequential confirmation.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: The platform interrupt sequence or explicit cancel stops at a documented safe boundary and reports retained, rolled-back, or resumable work.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: While work is pending, preserve responsive cancellation and status output, reject conflicting prompt input, and describe whether reconnect or retry is safe.

editing_matrix.surface: CLI arguments, stdin, interactive prompts, and command-line editing
editing_matrix.composition_behavior: Respect terminal or shell IME composition and do not interpret partial composed text as a choice, shortcut, delimiter, or submitted line.
editing_matrix.paste_autofill_behavior: Treat pasted, piped, repeated, multiline, and environment input through documented boundaries; never execute an incomplete pasted line or echo a secret.
editing_matrix.selection_caret_behavior: Preserve the editable buffer, cursor, history position, and prompt ownership through redraw, completion, resize, diagnostics, and cancellation.
editing_matrix.formatting_behavior: Parse locale and encoding deterministically, preserve machine-readable input exactly where promised, and defer normalization until after complete-token validation.
editing_matrix.validation_timing: Validate complete arguments or committed prompt input before side effects and distinguish parse, semantic, environmental, and per-item errors.
editing_matrix.validation_feedback: Write actionable sanitized errors to stderr with the offending field or argument, expected form, recovery command, and stable exit meaning.
editing_matrix.dirty_state_behavior: Identify buffered, confirmed, pending, written, and partially applied input so cancellation never implies uncommitted work was persisted.
editing_matrix.persistence_behavior: For interactive drafts, resumable files, or autosave, use explicit paths and atomic writes, preserve safe input after interruption, and report recovery ownership.
editing_matrix.undo_redo_behavior: Preserve shell or prompt history editing and provide explicit rollback or compensating commands for reversible committed changes.
editing_matrix.conflict_behavior: Detect changed files, stale revisions, locks, or concurrent command ownership before overwrite and require an explicit compare, retry, force, or alternate-output choice.
editing_matrix.read_only_disabled_behavior: Keep read-only values printable and copyable, reject disabled or unsupported options before side effects, and state the exact prerequisite without relying on color.
editing_matrix.submission_behavior: Define newline, end-of-input, confirmation, non-interactive, and interrupt semantics; reject duplicate submission and bind success to one authoritative exit and result.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: No input, records, files, or matches are available.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Emit an explicit empty outcome, distinguish it from failure, preserve a stable exit meaning, and name the next query, input, or creation step.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Representative and high-volume results include long identifiers and mixed statuses.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Preserve deterministic ordering, untruncated machine-readable values, bounded human output, and documented pagination or limit behavior.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Some items complete before per-item failure, timeout, signal, or dependency interruption.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Separate completed, skipped, pending, and failed identities; keep stdout parseable; and state safe retry or resume semantics.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Permission, authentication, configuration, network, storage, or dependency access fails.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Return a stable nonzero exit code, place sanitized diagnostics on stderr, preserve partial-work truth, and provide a concrete recovery command or prerequisite.

accessibility_matrix.surface: Command-line help, progress, results, and diagnostics
semantics: text equivalents for every visual cue
accessibility_matrix.reading_order: Output reads top-to-bottom in dependency order: outcome, affected scope, essential detail, recovery, then optional diagnostics.
accessibility_matrix.focus_order: The shell retains input ownership; interactive prompts present one current question at a time and return cleanly to the caller.
keyboard: Every operation is invokable, cancellable, and recoverable through documented command and keyboard input.
Interactive prompts support help, defaults, validation, end-of-input, and cancellation without trapping the terminal.
announcements: Use stable status words and line boundaries that screen readers can interpret.
Avoid continuously redrawing progress when accessibility or non-interactive output is selected.
accessibility_matrix.target_size: CLI interaction does not depend on pointer precision; each prompt choice is a complete text target with a documented key or command equivalent.
accessibility_matrix.contrast: Meaning never depends on color, and no-color output preserves the same status, hierarchy, and recovery information.
accessibility_matrix.zoom_reflow: Output wraps deterministically in narrow terminals and under enlarged terminal fonts without losing commands, identifiers, indentation meaning, or machine-readable records.
alternatives: Provide no-color and non-animated progress modes.
Provide stable line-oriented or structured output for screen readers, logging, and automation.

navigation_matrix.surface: CLI command tree and resumable workflow
navigation_matrix.entry: Executable, subcommand, help link, shell history, script, or documented resume command.
navigation_matrix.destination: The named subcommand, help topic, result, or resumable operation state.
navigation_matrix.trigger: Command invocation, explicit subcommand, help flag, or resume identifier.
navigation_matrix.back_behavior: Cancellation or a user error returns control to the shell without corrupting terminal state or implying rollback that did not occur.
navigation_matrix.deep_link_behavior: Documentation and diagnostics print a complete copyable command with required identifiers while omitting secrets and unstable local assumptions.
navigation_matrix.interruption_recovery: On signal, timeout, lost connection, or process restart, report the safe checkpoint, partial effects, cleanup need, and exact retry or resume command.

content_matrix.purpose: Make command intent, required input, result, and next action understandable to humans and automation.
content_matrix.copy: Use stable command names, verb-first summaries, realistic examples, and labels that remain meaningful without color or column alignment.
content_matrix.primary_action: Print the next copyable command only when it is valid for the returned state.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: State affected scope, dry-run or mutation mode, irreversible effects, result count, and authoritative completion truth.
content_matrix.localization: Keep command tokens stable while allowing translated prose, locale-aware human display, Unicode content, and explicitly locale-neutral machine output.
content_limits: Do not truncate identifiers or machine-readable fields.
Keep default human output bounded and move verbose diagnostics behind explicit flags.

content_matrix.purpose: Explain the failure boundary and provide a safe, copyable recovery route.
content_matrix.copy: Name the failed operation and sanitized cause, distinguish usage from environment and runtime failure, and identify retained or partial effects.
content_matrix.primary_action: Provide a concrete corrected, retry, resume, inspect, or cleanup command when one exists.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Never print secrets, invent rollback, claim success on partial failure, or make stderr/stdout ambiguous for automation.
content_matrix.localization: Keep error codes, option names, paths, and commands stable while prose and examples remain translatable and Unicode-safe.
content_limits: Show the essential cause and next action before stack traces or verbose logs.
Redact credentials, tokens, personal data, and unsafe command substitutions.

motion_contract.purpose: Represent progress and state change without cursor-dependent animation or output that becomes unstable when piped, logged, or read by assistive technology.

transitions.trigger: A long-running operation starts, advances, completes, fails, or is cancelled.
transitions.response: Use in-place progress only on an interactive TTY and emit stable milestone or final lines for piped, logged, no-animation, and accessibility modes.
transitions.interrupt_behavior: Cancellation stops redraw immediately, restores the cursor and terminal mode, then emits one authoritative partial-work and recovery outcome.

motion_contract.reduced_motion: Disable spinners and cursor animation, emit bounded textual milestones, and preserve identical exit, result, and recovery semantics.

methods: command grammar and help heuristic review
target-user task session in TTY, piped, narrow, and cancellation contexts
critical_tasks: Discover and run the primary command from help.
Consume the same successful result as human-readable and machine-readable output.
Diagnose and safely recover from invalid input, dependency failure, partial completion, and cancellation.
success_criteria: Users form a valid command without undocumented knowledge.
Scripts distinguish success, empty, partial, usage, and runtime failure through stable output and exit semantics.
Cancellation leaves terminal state clean and makes partial effects and recovery unambiguous.

targets.label: 80×24 terminal
targets.adaptation: Help, outcomes, and recovery instructions wrap without truncation or ambiguous indentation.
targets.stretch_behavior: Rewrap deterministically as columns shrink without changing command meaning, ordering, or exit semantics.
targets.overflow_behavior: Use stable wrapping, pagination only when interactive, and untruncated machine-readable output when piped.

targets.label: 120×32 terminal
targets.adaptation: Additional width improves scanability while preserving stable line-oriented and piped output.
targets.stretch_behavior: Use surplus columns for readable alignment without making semantics depend on terminal width.
targets.overflow_behavior: Keep long identifiers and diagnostics complete through wrapping or explicit continuation, never silent truncation.

profiles.label: Terminal user interface
profiles.summary: Cell-grid interactive terminal surfaces with explicit focus, keyboard navigation, resize behavior, overlays, and monochrome fallbacks.

specimens.title: Cell-grid workspace
specimens.purpose: Prove frame hierarchy, status line, readable density, and resize behavior in terminal cells.

specimens.title: Focus and keyboard navigation
specimens.purpose: Prove focus ownership, selection, shortcut language, and keyboard-only task completion.

specimens.title: Overlay, progress, and recovery
specimens.purpose: Prove modal boundaries, command palettes, progress, cancellation, and focus restoration.

data_scenarios.data_condition: The focused collection has no rows.
data_scenarios.expectation: Retain frame, focus ownership, commands, and an actionable empty explanation.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Representative and dense rows fill the available grid.
data_scenarios.expectation: Preserve selection, keyboard map, status meaning, and readable cell alignment.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Rows update progressively or a background operation remains pending.
data_scenarios.expectation: Identify pending regions without stealing focus or losing selection and scroll position.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Permission, connectivity, or a command fails.
data_scenarios.expectation: Keep the previous usable frame, restore focus after dismissal, and expose retry or recovery commands.

content_constraints: Fit command hints and essential status within the supported cell grid without hiding the focused task.
Wrap or scroll long values predictably and preserve full values in a detail or copy action.
component_contract.iconography: Use text labels and conventional terminal glyphs as redundant cues; retain complete meaning in monochrome, limited palettes, and fonts with missing glyphs.

interaction_matrix.surface: TUI workspace, panes, commands, and overlays
interaction_matrix.trigger: Tab, arrows, documented mnemonic or shortcut, Enter, Space, Escape, help, or cancellation key.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Decode complete terminal keydown-equivalent sequences, route them to the single active pane or overlay, and distinguish navigation, activation, command chords, Escape, and partial escape sequences.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Render visible focus, selection, command mode, pressed choice, validation, or pending status in the same refresh without relying on color alone.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Keep one visible focus owner, distinguish focus from selection, contain overlay focus, restore the invoker on close, and preserve the cursor through redraw and resize.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Use terminal key repeat only for documented navigation or continuous controls and suppress duplicate confirmation or destructive commands.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Escape or the cancellation key unwinds the nearest cancellable overlay, command mode, or operation while preserving buffers and restoring its invoker.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Keep the interface responsive to status, help, and safe cancel, block conflicting commands, and show whether work is queued, running, retryable, or resumable.

interaction_matrix.surface: TUI text input and command fields
interaction_matrix.trigger: Paste multiline or long text, resize the terminal, lose connection, or receive an interrupt while editing or running work.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Honor bracketed-paste start and end, complete escape sequences, resize events, connection loss, and interrupts without treating pasted newlines as unrelated commands.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Show the received buffer, validation boundary, truncation or sanitization decision, resize result, and connection status immediately without leaking secret input.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Preserve the active field, buffer, caret, selection, scroll region, and overlay owner across paste, resize, redraw, and reconnect.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Coalesce duplicate resize and connection events, preserve repeated literal pasted content, and prevent repeated interrupt or Enter events from committing twice.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: An interrupted paste, resize, disconnect, or cancel preserves the last complete buffer and committed state and names the safe resume or discard action.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: During processing or reconnect, keep status and safe cancellation available, reject conflicting commits, and restore the exact editing context when work resumes.

editing_matrix.surface: TUI text fields, filters, command palettes, and editable cells
editing_matrix.composition_behavior: Preserve terminal IME composition and suppress validation, shortcuts, navigation, and commit until the composed text is delivered as committed input.
editing_matrix.paste_autofill_behavior: Use bracketed-paste boundaries when available, confirm unsafe multiline input, preserve literal text, and never interpret paste as unrelated commands without consent.
editing_matrix.selection_caret_behavior: Keep buffer, cursor, selection, horizontal offset, focus owner, and cell position stable through redraw, resize, completion, and background output.
editing_matrix.formatting_behavior: Separate display clipping from stored input, preserve wide and combining characters, and defer normalization until a complete value is committed.
editing_matrix.validation_timing: Validate after committed input or the documented cell or form boundary, never during composition, and retain the editing buffer on error.
editing_matrix.validation_feedback: Show a persistent text error associated with the focused field, expose correction and help, and announce it through the terminal accessibility path without color alone.
editing_matrix.dirty_state_behavior: Distinguish clean, dirty, pending, saved, failed, and recovered buffers and intercept exit only when confirmed input would be lost.
editing_matrix.persistence_behavior: Manual save or autosave uses an explicit safe location, survives resize, disconnect, retry, and process interruption, and reports whether recovery is local or committed.
editing_matrix.undo_redo_behavior: Preserve text undo/redo and bounded application undo groups without losing the cursor, selection, or newer background state.
editing_matrix.conflict_behavior: Detect stale rows, changed files, or concurrent sessions before overwrite and offer inspect, compare, keep, reload, merge, or alternate-save recovery.
editing_matrix.read_only_disabled_behavior: Keep read-only text selectable where the terminal permits, skip disabled controls in activation, and state the reason and enabling command in text.
editing_matrix.submission_behavior: Define Enter, newline, apply, save, and cancel per control, prevent duplicate commits, preserve input on failure, and reconcile only the latest authoritative completion.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: The focused collection or filtered result has no rows.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Retain frame, focus, status, and applicable commands while distinguishing first-use from no-results and offering the next valid action.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Representative and dense rows fill the supported grid with long values and mixed statuses.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Preserve stable row identity, selection, keyboard map, readable alignment, and pane-local scroll position through updates and resize.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Rows arrive progressively or a background operation remains pending while other panes are usable.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Identify pending scope without stealing focus, keep usable panes interactive, and reject stale completion that would replace newer selection or input.

data_state_matrix.data_condition: Permission, connectivity, terminal capability, storage, or command execution fails.
data_state_matrix.expectation: Keep the prior usable frame, state the failure in text, restore focus after dismissal, and expose retry, inspect, cancel, or another recovery command.

accessibility_matrix.reading_order: A linearized mode and screen-reader reading order follow title, active context, focused pane, status, then commands without decorative cell noise.
accessibility_matrix.focus_order: Exactly one visible focus owner advances predictably between panes and overlays and returns to the invoker after dismissal.
keyboard: Every task and overlay is operable through documented keys with a discoverable help view.
Provide alternatives for mouse reporting, drag, function keys, and terminal-specific key chords.
announcements: Represent focus, selection, progress, errors, and completion in stable text.
Offer a reduced-redraw or linear mode so screen readers do not repeatedly announce the whole frame.
accessibility_matrix.target_size: TUI interaction does not require pointer precision; every actionable region has a documented key path and full-line or explicitly bounded focus target.
accessibility_matrix.contrast: Meaning remains complete in monochrome and limited palettes, with visible focus and selection independent of color alone.
accessibility_matrix.zoom_reflow: Respect enlarged terminal fonts and resize from supported minimum to wide grids without clipping focus, status, commands, or overlay boundaries.
alternatives: Provide monochrome, reduced-redraw, and linear text equivalents.
Provide non-mouse, non-color, non-glyph, and non-animation alternatives for every action and state.

navigation_matrix.surface: TUI panes, screens, command palette, and overlays
navigation_matrix.entry: Program launch, saved session, command argument, selected workspace, or documented resume invocation.
navigation_matrix.destination: The intended screen, pane, selection, overlay task, or recoverable operation state.
navigation_matrix.trigger: Keyboard navigation, command palette choice, shortcut, overlay action, or resume identifier.
navigation_matrix.back_behavior: Escape closes the top transient layer first, then returns to the prior meaningful context without discarding input or selection silently.
navigation_matrix.deep_link_behavior: Command arguments or resume identifiers select an authorized stable context and fall back to an explicit missing, expired, or permission outcome.
navigation_matrix.interruption_recovery: After resize, terminal reconnect, suspension, signal, or process restart, restore the last safe focus, selection, scroll, input, and operation checkpoint or clearly report what cannot be restored.

content_matrix.purpose: Make focus, selection, current context, commands, and status scannable within a constrained cell grid.
content_matrix.copy: Use stable short labels, verb-first commands, visible shortcut hints, and explicit status words that survive monochrome display.
content_matrix.primary_action: Expose the current primary command through both the focused control and a documented key.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Show affected scope, unsaved or pending state, destructive consequence, and authoritative completion status before leaving context.
content_matrix.localization: Handle Unicode width, right-to-left limitations explicitly, translated expansion, locale formats, and fonts without assumed glyph coverage.
content_limits: Never truncate the only distinguishing identifier or recovery command.
Use detail panes, wrapping, or copy actions for long values while keeping the primary grid stable.

content_matrix.surface: TUI error, cancellation, and unavailable states
content_matrix.purpose: Explain the affected scope and restore a usable keyboard path after failure or interruption.
content_matrix.copy: Name the failed command or region, retained state, partial effects, and next safe action in stable text.
content_matrix.primary_action: Offer retry, inspect, resume, save, undo, or return through an explicit key and visible label.
content_matrix.trust_requirement: Do not clear the prior frame, imply rollback, or report success until authoritative confirmation.
content_matrix.localization: Keep commands and keys stable while translating explanations and preserving readable cell width and line order.
content_limits: Show essential cause and recovery in the frame before optional logs.
Sanitize secrets and keep verbose diagnostics copyable outside the primary task grid.

motion_contract.purpose: Communicate progress and state change through stable cell updates that remain usable in reduced-redraw, monochrome, remote, and assistive contexts.

transitions.surface: TUI focus, overlays, progress, and frame updates
transitions.trigger: Focus moves, an overlay opens or closes, progress advances, data updates, or the grid resizes.
transitions.response: Update only affected cells when possible and preserve an equivalent stable-text state without animation.
transitions.interrupt_behavior: A new key, resize, reconnect, or cancellation stops transient redraw, preserves input and focus ownership, and renders one authoritative current state.

motion_contract.reduced_motion: Use a reduced-redraw or linear mode with static status text, no spinner animation, and identical focus, result, error, and recovery meaning.

methods: target-user task session at 80x24 and 120x40 with resize and reconnect stress
critical_tasks: Discover focus and complete the primary command without mouse input.
Operate overlays, long input, and dense collections at the minimum grid.
Recover focus and work after resize, cancellation, reconnect, and a command failure.
success_criteria: Users always identify focus, selection, current context, and the next command.
Minimum-grid and monochrome operation preserve every critical action and status.
Resize and interruption do not corrupt input, steal focus, or obscure partial effects and recovery.

targets.label: 80×24 TUI
targets.adaptation: The primary pane, focus, commands, and status remain visible at the minimum supported grid.
targets.stretch_behavior: Collapse secondary panes as the grid shrinks while preserving focus, selection, overlay ownership, and active input.
targets.overflow_behavior: Use pane-local scrolling and concise status text; never render controls outside the grid or hide recovery commands.

targets.label: 120×40 TUI
targets.adaptation: Secondary context expands without changing focus order, command meaning, or cell alignment.
targets.stretch_behavior: Expand approved panes and detail context without changing keyboard order, focus owner, or selection.
targets.overflow_behavior: Keep dense panes independently scrollable and maintain status, command hints, and overlay boundaries.

profiles.label: Content-led experience
profiles.summary: Editorial, documentation, publishing, or reading experiences where hierarchy, measure, media, localization, and print flow are the product surface.

specimens.title: Editorial hierarchy and reading rhythm
specimens.purpose: Prove title, deck, body, headings, links, lists, code, and readable measure with real-length content.

specimens.title: Media, caption, and fallback
specimens.purpose: Prove image or illustration framing, captions, attribution, missing-media fallback, and semantic reading order.

specimens.title: Localization and print flow
specimens.purpose: Prove text expansion, tables, callouts, footnotes, page breaks, and print-safe hierarchy.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Primary content or media is absent.
data_scenarios.expectation: Preserve semantic structure and show a meaningful fallback or next action without decorative gaps.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Representative long-form content and media are present.
data_scenarios.expectation: Maintain reading measure, hierarchy, navigation, and media relationships.

data_scenarios.data_condition: Content expands through localization, tables, callouts, and long unbroken values.
data_scenarios.expectation: Reflow without overlap, truncation, or loss of semantic order.

data_scenarios.data_condition: A media asset, permission, or remote content source is unavailable.
data_scenarios.expectation: Provide accessible fallback meaning and recovery while retaining the surrounding reading context.

content_constraints: Maintain readable measure and hierarchy with long-form, translated, and user-generated content.
Preserve captions, attribution, alternatives, footnotes, code, and tables without overlap or semantic reordering.
component_contract.iconography: Use restrained, labeled icons only for navigation or actions; editorial meaning, attribution, warnings, and media alternatives remain complete in text.

interaction_matrix.surface: Content navigation, links, media, disclosures, and annotations
interaction_matrix.trigger: Click a link, disclosure, footnote, media control, table affordance, or in-page navigation target.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve pointerdown, selection or scroll movement, and pointerup/click so selection, drag, and scrolling do not become accidental navigation; pointercancel leaves the reading state unchanged.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Expose hover or pressed state, destination, disclosure state, media status, or annotation target immediately without hiding the underlying text.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Preserve the reading anchor, text selection, focus visibility, and return point when following footnotes, disclosures, previews, or transient media controls.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Distinguish double-click text selection, repeated media controls, and repeated link activation; prevent duplicate navigation or download while preserving intentional stepping.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Pointercancel, selection movement, Escape from a preview, or invalid drag restores the prior reading anchor and removes only transient content.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Keep the source context and loading status visible, prevent duplicate navigation or download, and expose safe cancel, retry, or return behavior.

interaction_matrix.surface: Content navigation, links, media, disclosures, and annotations
interaction_matrix.trigger: Navigate headings, landmarks, links, controls, tables, footnotes, or search results and activate with standard keys.
interaction_matrix.event_sequence: Resolve keydown/keyup or assistive activation through native link, disclosure, media, table, and in-page navigation semantics exactly once.
interaction_matrix.immediate_feedback: Keep focus visible and expose expanded, visited, playing, paused, loading, or annotation state immediately with an appropriate accessible announcement.
interaction_matrix.focus_behavior: Follow semantic reading order, preserve the reading anchor, and restore focus after footnotes, transient content, search results, or media controls close.
interaction_matrix.repeat_behavior: Ignore repeat for one-shot navigation and downloads while allowing documented media seek, table navigation, and reading-control repetition.
interaction_matrix.cancellation_behavior: Escape or the documented back action closes the nearest transient content, stops cancellable media or loading, and returns to the invoking reading anchor.
interaction_matrix.pending_behavior: Announce pending content once, retain a stable reading and focus position, prevent duplicate activation, and provide retry or return without requiring hover, drag, color, or spatial memory.

editing_matrix.surface: Content search, annotations, comments, publishing metadata, and editorial fields when present
editing_matrix.composition_behavior: Preserve IME composition and reading position and defer validation, formatting, shortcuts, search execution, or publishing actions until composition commits.
editing_matrix.paste_autofill_behavior: Accept pasted citations, links, rich text, metadata, autofill, and dictation through a visible sanitization policy without silently losing meaning or provenance.
editing_matrix.selection_caret_behavior: Preserve caret, selection, annotation anchor, reading position, and text direction through preview, references, asynchronous suggestions, and layout reflow.
editing_matrix.formatting_behavior: Keep source meaning and partial input intact, separate semantic markup from visual presentation, and defer destructive normalization until an explicit commit or preview boundary.
editing_matrix.validation_timing: Do not validate during composition; validate links, metadata, structure, and publishing constraints at a documented field, preview, or publish boundary.
editing_matrix.validation_feedback: Associate errors with source fields and affected preview content, state a correction, preserve the value, and announce material changes without resetting the reading anchor.
editing_matrix.dirty_state_behavior: Distinguish draft, dirty, autosaving, saved, failed, scheduled, and published state and warn only when navigation would discard confirmed editorial work.
